**Level:** Graduate (Master's)

**Time:** 6:00 PM - 8:15 PM (Wednesdays)

**Term:** Spring 2026

**Instructor:** Sangsuk Yoon (syoon1\@udayton.edu)

# Course Description and Objectives:

## Course Description:

This graduate-level course provides a comprehensive introduction to business analytics in healthcare management, progressing from basic statistical concepts and data visualization to practical applications of data analytics in healthcare management decisions. As healthcare organizations increasingly rely on data-driven insights, this course prepares students to navigate and analyze complex healthcare datasets. Students will gain hands-on experience with classic and modern analytical tools while learning to address real-world healthcare management challenges through evidence-based decision-making.

## Prerequisites:

There are no prerequisites for this course. This course is designed to accommodate students with varying levels of statistical and programming background. All necessary concepts will be introduced from the ground up.

## Course Objectives:

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

-   Evaluate the role and application of analytics in healthcare management decision-making
-   Conduct exploratory data analysis on different types of healthcare data (patient surveys, health outcomes, etc.)
-   Select and apply appropriate statistical methods to healthcare management problems to extract meaningful insights
-   Interpret analytical results and communicate findings effectively to diverse stakeholders
-   Design and implement data-driven solutions for real-world healthcare management challenges

## R and R-Studio:

This course utilizes R and R-Studio as the primary analytical tools. R is a powerful, open-source programming language specifically designed for statistical data analysis, widely used in both academia and industry for analytics. R-Studio is an integrated development environment (IDE) that makes R programming more accessible and efficient through its user-friendly interface, offering features such as data visualization, code editing, debugging, and project management capabilities. Students will learn to use these tools to analyze healthcare data, create visualizations, develop statistical models, and generate reports. You can download R and R-Studio from the following links:

-   R: <https://www.r-project.org>
-   R-Studio: <https://posit.co/downloads/>

**You should install R first since R-Studio runs on R.**

## Assignments: 100 points (10 assignments, each with 10 points)

There will be 10 assignments throughout the semester. Each assignment requires students to apply the analytical methods learned in the class session to new healthcare data analytics scenarios. For example, in Week 4, after we cover data visualization, you will be asked to visualize results with a new dataset. Assignments will focus on different healthcare management contexts and typically take 30-60 minutes to complete. Assignments are due weekly by Sunday at 11:59 PM.

## Class Participation and Reflection: 78 points

This course includes 14 class sessions. After we finish each session (starting from the second class), I would like to hear about what you learned and what questions remain unclear. To encourage engagement with the course contents, you will need to write a short list of responses to the following questions:

1.  **What were the three most interesting or exciting things you learned from the session? and why?**
2.  **What were the three most unclear or confusing things from the session? and why?**

You can include more than three for each, but you must include at least three per question. So, there are six interesting or unclear things you will have in each reflection, and each one will worth 1 point (total 6 points per class session; max is 6 points). There will be 13 reflection assignments throughout the semester (6 points × 13 reflections = 78 points). Reflection submissions are due weekly by Sunday at 11:59 PM.

## Midterm Exam: 50 points

There will be a midterm exam in Week 9 of the semester. The exam will cover topics covered from Week 1 through Week 8. The exam will be online, and students need to complete it within 24 hours.

## Final Exam: 50 points

There will be a final exam in the last week of the semester. The exam will be cumulative and cover what we cover in class this semester. The exam will be online, and students need to complete within 24 hours.

# Class Policies

## Attendance Policy:

This course is delivered online synchronously, and attendance is required. Attendance will be measured before or middle of each class at random. If you miss more than three class sessions, you cannot pass this course (= your grade will be F). Missing class does not relieve your responsibility for assignments, reflection, or exams.

## Communication Policy:

-   All course-related communication should be sent to my UD email: syoon1\@udayton.edu
-   I will do my best to respond to emails within 24 hours during weekdays (Monday-Friday)
-   Please note that emails sent during weekends, holidays, or university breaks may receive delayed responses

## Classroom Etiquette:

-   TURN ON the camera during class time to facilitate engagement and interaction.
-   Treat class time as a meeting in current/future professional life.
-   Show respect for yourself, your peers, and our school; behave in a civil and appropriate manner for a school of business.
-   Professional language is required in all class discussions and written assignments.

## Technological Problems:

-   Students are responsible for ensuring reliable internet connectivity when joining the class and submitting assignments.
-   All students must maintain an active UD email account and Zoom and Canvas access.
-   Technical issues with personal computers or software (including R and R-Studio) are the student’s responsibility.
-   For hardware issues, contact your device manufacturer. For software issues, contact UD IT services. I will provide guidance on course-specific technical matters when possible.

## Late Submissions:

A late submission is subject to the following policy:

-   **Reflections**: a 1.5-point reduction from the points you earn will apply for each 24-hour period past the deadline. Reflections submitted more than 48 hours late will receive zero points.
-   **Assignments**: a 2-point reduction from the points you earn will apply for each 24-hour period past the deadline. Assignments submitted more than 48 hours late will receive zero points.
-   **Exams**: Exams must be completed within the specified time frame. No late submissions will be accepted for exams.

## Retaining Assignments and Research Exercises:

-   Students must keep a copy of each Assignment and any related documents. In the unlikely event that an Assignment or Research Exercise is misplaced or cannot be found, the onus is on you to provide a backup copy of the assignment.
-   In addition, you must keep your graded assignments. Any queries concerning the awarded grade (e.g., a discrepancy between what is posted on Canvas and what is on your paper) can only be resolved with the original assignment document.

## Check Grades:

Students are responsible for regularly monitoring their grades on Canvas. If you think an assignment that you handed in was not graded, or that the grade that was posted is wrong, feel free to reach out to me for review and verification.

## Academic Honesty

You are expected to do your own written work on all assignments and projects. For specific UD policies concerning academic honesty, see the University’s Academic Honor Code in the Academic Catalog.

## Contract Cheating

Contract cheating occurs when a student pays someone (such as a person or company found online) to write essays or complete assignments for a class. This defeats the purpose of the course, and I encourage you to follow the academic honor code and seek to develop a personal sense of academic integrity which lays the foundation for an ethical life. Contract cheating is especially dangerous because of the risk of bribery and extortion (at any point after after college.) Students are often lured into contract cheating by signing up for online tutoring services. Remember that UD provides many learning support resources through the Office of Learning Resources.

## Academic Integrity and ChatGPT/AI Generated Content

As a student at UD, you are expected to adhere to the Standards of Conduct outlined in the Academic Honor Code. One of the goals for your educational development is to develop your critical thinking and writing skills, which can be weakened by regularly utilizing AI for writing. Thus, for this course, all submitted writing should be your own, original work. If you quote or copy content from ChatGPT or other AI sources, it must be appropriately cited in your submissions. As your instructor, I am required to investigate all suspected violations of academic dishonesty and follow the honor code violation procedures, which can result in an NC for the course.

## Dropping the Course

You are responsible for understanding the University’s policies and procedures regarding withdrawing from courses. You should also be aware of the current deadlines and penalties for dropping classes. Information on withdrawal from courses is available in the Academic Catalog under Grades and Scholarship. You may also want to speak with your academic advisor.
